In this release, history is restored in small slices instead of one long blocking task, so the window stays responsive. Opening, switching back to, and reloading large chats is significantly faster. additions: H1: Visual Studio Code 1.143
Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Instagram
Last updated: October 19, 2026
Welcome to the 1.143 release of Visual Studio Code.
H2: Downloads for 1.143.0
This release makes the Copilot harness the default for new sessions and adds tools to compare models, reclaim storage, run models locally, and navigate file changes.
Copilot harness by default: The default for new sessions, built on the Copilot SDK, lets you switch between editor and Agents window.
Compare models (Preview): Run the same task with multiple models in the Agents window, then compare and combine their solutions.
Reclaim worktree storage (Experimental): Free disk space by reviewing and removing inactive agent session worktrees.
On-device models (Experimental): Run MAI Code 1.1 Flash locally on your device for your agent tasks.
Multi-diff file list (Experimental): Keep an overview of and jump between changed files in the multi-file diff editor.
H3: Copilot harness as the default

The Copilot harness is now the default for new sessions in VS Code. It's our latest harness, built on the Copilot SDK, a shared foundation that helps align behavior, capabilities, and improvements across Copilot products.
When you start a new session, Copilot in the harness picker indicates that the session uses the Copilot harness:
In VS Code, you can keep Copilot harness sessions running in the background and access them from both the VS Code editor window and the Agents window. These sessions run through the Agent Host.
